clue.text: Cleaner male helps holding decoration for cleaners

indicators.note: holding means the first string of letters wraps around the decoration's letters

parts.note: a char is a cleaning lady, a charwoman
the MBE (Member of the Order of the British Empire) is a British honour or decoration
aids means helps

explanation.surface: A cleaner and a man help out, carrying an ornament for the cleaning staff.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Cleaner' looks like the definition, but it is wordplay; the definition is the plural 'cleaners' at the end. The MBE is a British honour.
explanation.definitionFit: Chambermaids are hotel staff who clean and tidy the bedrooms, so they are cleaners.

clue.text: Enclosure surrounds extravagant country residence

indicators.note: surrounds means the enclosure's letters go around the next piece

parts.note: a cage is an enclosure for animals
OTT, over the top, means extravagant

explanation.surface: A walled enclosure encircles a lavish house in the countryside.
explanation.definitionFit: A cottage is a small house in the country, a rural dwelling.

clue.text: One can see one's behind in these!

definitions.text: One can see one's behind in these!

parts.words: One can see one's behind in these!
parts.note: the picture is of a mirror or seat that shows a person's backside, but being behind with payments means being in debt owed past its due date

explanation.surface: A cheeky line about something that lets you view your own bottom.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Behind' reads as one's rear, but it means late with payments: someone who is behind is 'in' the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: Money overdue and still unpaid; a debtor who is behind with payments is said to be in them.

clue.text: Spectator beside street also overlooks Queen

indicators.note: in a down clue, overlooks puts the preceding letters above the queen's

parts.note: by means beside, as in 'sit by me'
and means also
ER, Elizabeth Regina, is the Queen

explanation.surface: Someone watches from beside a road that also looks out over the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: A bystander is an onlooker who watches an event without taking part.

clue.text: Mad charge round beginning of Balaclava

indicators.note: round means the attack's letters are placed around the next piece

parts.note: a raid is a charge or sudden attack

indicators.note: beginning of takes just the opening letter of Balaclava

explanation.surface: A crazed cavalry charge at the start of the Battle of Balaclava, recalling the Light Brigade.
explanation.definitionFit: Rabid means furious or fanatical, as well as having rabies; both senses fit mad.

clue.text: American Native Americans covering a grand expanse

indicators.note: covering means the people's name wraps around the next letters

parts.note: the Cree are a Native American people
G stands for grand, a thousand dollars or pounds

explanation.surface: An American and some indigenous peoples spread across a vast territory.
explanation.definitionFit: Acreage is an area of land measured in acres, an extent or expanse of ground.

clue.text: Present turned up, first of skimpy pants

indicators.note: turned up, in a down clue, means the word for present is read from bottom to top

parts.note: to reward someone is to present them with something

indicators.note: first of takes the opening letter of skimpy

explanation.surface: A gift is unwrapped: the first item being some skimpy underwear.
explanation.definitionFit: Drawers is an old word for knickers or underpants, which are pants in British usage.

clue.text: Span Arctic if at sea spanning an ocean

indicators.note: at sea means confused or all over the place, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A bridge across the Arctic, if out on the water, would cross a whole ocean.
explanation.walkthrough: 'at sea' signals an anagram of SPAN ARCTIC IF.
explanation.definitionFit: Transpacific describes something crossing the Pacific, so it means spanning that ocean.

clue.text: Concerned with time machine forgetting one decelerates

parts.note: re means concerning or with regard to

indicators.note: forgetting means a piece is left out of the time machine's name

parts.note: the TARDIS is Doctor Who's time machine in the BBC science-fiction series
I is the Roman numeral one

explanation.surface: A story about a time machine that forgets something and slows down.
explanation.walkthrough: 'forgetting one' removes I from TARDIS, leaving TARDS. The TARDIS is the time-travelling police box from the BBC's Doctor Who.
explanation.definitionFit: To retard something is to slow it, so a thing that retards it decelerates it.

clue.text: Attack in anger following boozer

indicators.note: following puts the anger word after the pub word

parts.note: a boozer is a pub, so a bar
rage means anger

explanation.surface: A furious assault breaks out after a session at the pub.
explanation.definitionFit: A barrage is a heavy, concentrated bombardment, an onslaught of fire or words.

clue.text: Grasping former partner, wrong to tear into

parts.note: an ex is a former partner

indicators.note: wrong means the letters of to tear into are set wrongly, rearranged

explanation.surface: A greedy ex-partner who wrongly wants to rip into someone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wrong' makes TORTIONATE from the letters of TO TEAR INTO. 'Wrong' also looks like TORT, a decoy.
explanation.definitionFit: Extortionate means charging far too much, which is greedy or grasping.

clue.text: A fall, around a gallon going over falls

indicators.note: around means the reversed letters go round the next pair
going over means the letters of a and fall are turned back to front

parts.note: rain is a fall, of water from the sky
taken as written

explanation.surface: One tumble over a gallon of water heading over a waterfall.
explanation.walkthrough: 'A fall' sounds like a tumble, yet it is rain; 'going over' turns it to NIARA, and the gallon pair sits inside that.
explanation.definitionFit: Niagara is the famous waterfall on the US–Canada border, a set of falls.

clue.text: Some of multitude are strangely most excessive

indicators.note: Some of says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A sizeable part of a crowd is oddly over the top.
explanation.walkthrough: 'strangely' looks like an anagram signal, but it is only fodder.
explanation.definitionFit: Dearest means most expensive, so the price that is most excessive.

clue.text: Verses from American writer with manuscript

indicators.note: with puts the manuscript next to the writer

parts.note: Edgar Allan Poe was an American writer

explanation.surface: Lines of poetry taken from an American author's handwritten papers.
explanation.definitionFit: Poems are compositions in verse, so verses in a broad sense.

clue.text: I press end energetically for its contents?

definitions.text: I press end energetically for its contents?

indicators.note: energetically suggests vigorous jumbling, so the letters of I press end are rearranged

explanation.surface: Someone pushes hard on the end of something to get out what is inside.
explanation.walkthrough: 'energetically' signals an anagram of I PRESS END; the whole clue also describes using a pump bottle of soap.
explanation.definitionFit: A dispenser is a device that releases its contents when you push it, like a soap pump.

clue.text: Second role play cut American in 'Gladiator'

parts.note: a part is a role

indicators.note: cut means the final letter is lopped off

parts.note: to act is to play a part

explanation.surface: A supporting part in the film Gladiator, with an American's scene trimmed.
explanation.definitionFit: Spartacus was the Thracian gladiator who led the slave revolt against Rome.

clue.text: Restaurant is about carnival atmosphere returning

parts.note: ca, circa, means about
a fete is a carnival or fair

indicators.note: returning means the word for atmosphere is read backwards

parts.note: air means atmosphere, as in the mood of a place

explanation.surface: A restaurant is said to have something of a festival feel coming back.
explanation.definitionFit: A cafeteria is a self-service eatery, a kind of restaurant.

clue.text: Peculiar France first off overthrew monarchy

parts.note: F is the international vehicle code for France

indicators.note: first off takes the opening letter of overthrew

parts.note: a reign is a monarch's rule

explanation.surface: A strange tale: France was the first to topple its monarchy.
explanation.walkthrough: 'overthrew' is not an indicator; only its first letter is used.
explanation.definitionFit: Foreign can mean strange or alien, as in 'foreign to his nature'.

clue.text: Orchestra cheated pinching inspirational passage?

indicators.note: pinching means the words grip the answer inside them, across the gap between them

explanation.surface: The orchestra cheated by stealing a stirring section of music.
explanation.walkthrough: 'inspirational' puns on breathing in: a passage used for inspiration.
explanation.definitionFit: The windpipe is the passage air goes through when inhaling, inspiration in the breathing sense.

clue.text: Dog collar on rector gets itchy initially

indicators.note: initially means take the first letter of each of the following words

explanation.surface: A clergyman's dog collar makes him scratch.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Dog collar' looks like one phrase; 'Dog' is the definition and 'collar' starts the run.
explanation.definitionFit: The corgi is a short-legged Welsh breed of dog, favoured by Queen Elizabeth II.

clue.text: Criminal ready for pardon

parts.note: a con, a convict, is a criminal
done means ready, as food that is cooked

explanation.surface: A lawbreaker is all set for his release.
explanation.definitionFit: To condone is to overlook or forgive an offence, much like pardoning it.

clue.text: Clothing is torn catching end

indicators.note: catching means the word for torn holds the next word inside

parts.note: rent means torn, as in a garment rent apart
an aim is an end, a goal

explanation.surface: A garment gets ripped when its end snags.
explanation.definitionFit: Raiment is an old literary word for garments or clothing.

clue.text: Forge mug gripping container

indicators.note: gripping means the word for mug holds the container inside it

parts.note: mug is slang for face
an urn is a container

explanation.surface: A blacksmith's workshop where a mug holds a vessel.
explanation.definitionFit: A forge is a smith's hearth, an enclosed fire for heating metal, so a furnace.

clue.text: Repaired without Mike getting wound up

indicators.note: without means the letter for Mike is dropped

parts.note: mended means repaired
Mike is M in the NATO phonetic alphabet

explanation.surface: Something is fixed with no help from Mike, which annoys him.
explanation.walkthrough: 'wound up' looks like annoyed but means concluded.
explanation.definitionFit: Wound up means concluded or finished.

clue.text: Sergeant-major's order said to create conflict

indicators.note: said means the word is spoken, so we want a word sounding like it

parts.note: a sergeant-major barks 'Attention!', clipped on the parade ground to 'Tenshun!'

explanation.surface: A drill sergeant's barked command can stir up strife.
explanation.definitionFit: Tension is strain or hostility between people, a state of conflict.

clue.text: Tired head of Church prevaricated about Church

indicators.note: head of takes the first letter of Church
about means the word for prevaricated goes around the next letters

parts.note: to prevaricate is to evade the truth, so lied

explanation.surface: A weary church leader dodged questions about the church.
explanation.definitionFit: Tired in the sense of stale or hackneyed, as an overused phrase is.

clue.text: Most intimate undies finally put in wardrobe

indicators.note: put in means that letter goes inside the wardrobe word

parts.note: a closet is a cupboard or wardrobe

indicators.note: finally takes the last letter of undies

explanation.surface: The most private underwear ends up stowed in the wardrobe.
explanation.definitionFit: Closest friends are the dearest and nearest, the most intimate.

clue.text: Glowing with wearing unusually nice perfume

indicators.note: wearing means the shuffled letters have the next word on, around it
unusually means the letters of nice are arranged in an unusual order

parts.note: and means with, together with
a scent is a perfume

explanation.surface: Someone is radiant while wearing an unusually pleasant fragrance.
explanation.walkthrough: 'with' is not a link word here but supplies letters; 'unusually' gives INCE, which 'wearing' wraps round them.
explanation.definitionFit: Incandescent means emitting light because of great heat, so glowing.
